Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State.
This is an appeal under section 101(5) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,
2015 in connection with Kodinga P.S. Case No.211 of 2021 corresponding to C.T. Case No.03 of 2022 pending in the Court of learned Addl. Sessions Judge - cum- Judge, Children's Court, Nabarangpur for // 2 // offences punishable under sections 376(3)/376(2)(n) /506 of the Indian Penal Code read with section 4(2)/6 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant is detained in observation home since 31.12.2021 and in the meantime, in the trial court, out of thirtyone charge sheeted witnesses,
twentyseven witnesses have been examined and both the victim and the appellant are of same age and it appears that there was intimacy between them and they kept physical relationship.

Learned counsel placed the evidence of the victim who was examined as P.W.1 and submitted that in view of the period of detention of the appellant, progress of the trial and nature of evidence adduced so far in the trial court, the bail application of the appellant may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand submitted that the victim has delivered a baby girl who was aged about one month when she deposed in the trial Court on 21st May 2023.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the age of the appellant, his period of detention in observation // 3 // home, nature of evidence adduced so far in the trial Court and the progress of trial so far, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Let the appellant be released on bail in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as the learned Court in seisin over the matter may deem just and proper with further conditions that:-
(i) one surety should be the family member of the appellant, who shall furnish an undertaking that the appellant shall not be allowed to come in contact with any unsocial and criminal association and shall not be exposed to any moral, physical or psychological danger and further he shall ensure that the appellant is not indulged in any criminal activities and he shall further ensure the presence of the appellant during trial before the Court as and when required;

(ii) the District Probation Officer shall keep a close vigilance on the activities of the appellant while on bail and regularly draw his social investigation report which shall be submitted to the Court on periodical basis as the Court chooses.
The CRLA is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of this order on proper application.
